back: Plant or animal material (dung, compost, green manure) added to soil for nutrients and organic matter.
Dark, crumbly material made when micro-organisms decompose plant and animal wastes in a heap or pit.
A crop, usually a legume such as sunn hemp, ploughed in while green (about flowering).

front: Steps in making a compost heap
back: Shaded level site → coarse base → layers of plant material, manure and soil → water → cover → turn after about 3 weeks → ready in 2-3 months.

front: Why does a compost heap get hot?
back: Respiration of micro-organisms decomposing the material; up to about 60 °C, killing weed seeds and pathogens.

front: Effects of organic matter on soil
back: Better crumb structure, more water and nutrients held, more soil life, steadier pH, less erosion.
Rhizobium in root nodules fixes nitrogen; rotting legume residues leave nitrogen for the next crop.
Organic: cheap, slow, bulky, low analysis, builds soil. Inorganic: concentrated, fast, known analysis, costly, no organic matter.
Ploughing in carbon-rich residues (dry maize stalks) lets microbes use soil nitrogen for a while, so crops turn pale.
